research_rationale:
EO 11726 (June 29, 1973) established the Energy Policy Office in the Executive Office of the President under a Director, set the Director's responsibilities, provided expenses and support, set a report date of March 15, 1974, and superseded EO 11712 (abolishing the Special Committee on Energy and the National Energy Office). EO 11748 of December 4, 1973 (Federal Energy Office) superseded EO 11726 only "to the extent that it is inconsistent" with it. EO 11775 of March 26, 1974 states that the Energy Policy Office was continued in being on an interim basis to permit an orderly transition, and abolishes it and supersedes EO 11726 in its Section 1. The status is NO: the Office was abolished and the order superseded on March 26, 1974, and no held source revives it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The partial supersession by EO 11748 Sec. 6 (December 4, 1973) reaches only provisions inconsistent with EO 11748, and no held source identifies which clause of EO 11726 it extinguished: EO 11775 itself recites that the Energy Policy Office was continued on an interim basis after EO 11748 until the transition was completed. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 an endpoint needs a reason shown by evidence, so EO 11748 is recorded as a later event (partial supersession), not a first end, and the first established end of every clause is EO 11775, March 26, 1974. No own-terms end exists: the March 15, 1974 report date in Sec. 4 is a deadline, not an end. A formal reviewer should note the possibility that some clauses were displaced between December 4, 1973 and March 26, 1974; the held evidence does not show it.","independent_command_check":"Sec. 5 (supersedure of EO 11712 and abolition of the Special Committee on Energy and the National Energy Office) is a one-time self-executing command performed on June 29, 1973, so its first end is the signing date, not the later abolition of the Energy Policy Office. savings.reason: EO 11775 Sec. 2 amends Section 8 of Proclamation No. 3279 so that the Administrator of the Federal Energy Office chairs the Oil Policy Committee, continues the Committee as reconstituted, and transfers personnel, property, records and funds for the functions moved from the Director of the Energy Policy Office; Sec. 3 directs the Administrator of General Services to wind up the Office and return unobligated funds to the Emergency Fund of the President. Those functions and funds accrue to the Federal Energy Office and the Fund; no other EO 11726 command is preserved.
